page.title: Board
page.purpose: Be the one address a member starts from: the ranked error surface, with enough qualification visible that no number can be read as more confident than it is.

regions.purpose: State the setpoint's own confidence and the open-loop count before any ranked finding is shown, so completeness is never implied by omission.

Present the merged error surface in rank order — out-of-band readings, untrusted readings, open-loop cells, coverage drift and source unavailability — each labelled with the named source it came from.
Show every degraded or unreadable source with its stated reason, so a short board reads as a partial board rather than a healthy one.

states.description: Every source readable and every target in band. The header still shows setpoint confidence and the open-loop count, because in-band is not the same as fully measured.
Findings present and ordered, with trust findings ranked above plant findings per the cascade rule.
One or more sources unreadable. Healthy sources keep ranking; each unreadable source appears in the availability region with its reason verbatim.
No findings. Must be distinguishable at a glance from 'nothing could be read' — an empty board and a blind board are different claims.
The setpoint itself could not be read or parsed. The board reports the failure and refuses to show a target count it does not have.
The board is loading its setpoint and source readings.
The board is showing the last known reading while a refresh is pending.
A board request failed and the failure is visible.

priorities.statement: A reader must never mistake an unavailable source for a healthy one.
priorities.notes: The single most consequential failure this surface can have. Degradation is always visible and always carries its stated reason.

priorities.statement: No ratio appears without the confidence or trust qualifier that makes it honest.
priorities.notes: Mirrors the recursive-honesty rule in SETPOINT-MODEL.md: 'X of Y in band, against a PARTIAL setpoint'.

priorities.statement: Status is never carried by colour alone.
priorities.notes: The whole surface is status, so the accessibility floor matters more here than on a typical page. Every verdict pairs a hue with a label or shape.

claims.statement: When any sensor source is unreadable, the availability region names that source and its stated reason, and the board does not present its cells as in band.
claims.rationale: The degradation contract in TARGET_MODEL.md: an unreadable source becomes a visible availability entry, never a zero and never a silently dropped row.

claims.statement: A reading with a non-VALID trust verdict is shown as untrusted and is excluded from any in-band aggregate on the page.
claims.rationale: TRUST-MODEL.md honesty invariant — an untrusted reading is not evidence and must not be totalled as if it were.

claims.statement: The empty state is visually and textually distinct from the error state.
claims.rationale: 'No findings' and 'nothing could be read' are opposite claims; conflating them is the exact failure the availability region exists to prevent.

claims.statement: Every status indicator pairs its colour with a text label or distinct shape, and meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast in both themes.
claims.rationale: The page is entirely status; colour-only encoding would make it unusable for colour-blind operators.
